about: Signal is a free quarterly briefing from Yroc Consulting for our clients and friends on how AI is changing the way customers find businesses. Every stat is sourced: tap a source to read it.

letter.title: The front desk moved.
body: For twenty years, being found meant showing up on Google. This quarter, that changed in a way you can actually see: ChatGPT now lets businesses claim a profile, Google's AI Mode reads more of the web than before, and Google Maps will even call a business to book an appointment for a customer.

None of this replaces the basics. It raises the stakes on them. AI tools recommend businesses they can clearly identify, verify and trust, which means accurate profiles, real reviews and pages that answer the questions customers actually ask.

In this issue we've pulled together what changed, why it matters to a business like yours, and what we'd do about it this quarter. If something here raises a question, bring it to your next call. That's what we're here for.

news_title: Eight moves that changed how customers find you

news.headline: ChatGPT now has its own business profiles
news.what: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT on November 10. Owners can claim a profile, edit hours, services and products, and see how often ChatGPT mentions them.
news.why: It's the first official way to shape how ChatGPT describes your business, and ChatGPT reaches 1.2 billion people a week. Claiming is free. Make it match your Google profile exactly.

news.headline: A smarter AI Mode that links to more sites
news.what: Google made its new Gemini model the default in AI Mode worldwide on November 12, and says answers now connect people to a broader range of websites, with more tables and comparisons.
news.why: AI Mode breaks each question into smaller ones. Pages that answer specific questions about price, service area, process and timing get more chances to be cited.

news.headline: Google's AI will call businesses to book appointments
news.what: Ask Maps can now check availability and phone local businesses for the customer, starting in the US with beauty, pet care, auto and home repair.
news.why: Accurate hours, online booking and staff ready for an automated call now decide whether the AI sends you the customer or the shop down the street.

news.headline: The November core update is rolling out
news.what: Google began its third core update of 2026 on November 10. Google said it may take up to two weeks to finish.
news.why: Rankings can swing during a rollout. Judge the results in December, once it has settled, not in the middle of it.

news.headline: An AI agent that answers your customers' messages
news.what: Google is giving more businesses early access to AI messaging: customers text from Search and Maps, an AI answers routine questions, and harder ones go to the owner.
news.why: Whatever your profile says becomes the script the AI works from. Outdated hours or services mean wrong answers in your name.

news.headline: Ads are moving into AI answers
news.what: On its October earnings call, Google said it is scaling ads within AI Overviews and AI Mode, and that AI Mode questions are on average three times longer than traditional searches.
news.why: Paid slots will sit beside the businesses AI recommends for free. Being the one it recommends on its own is worth more every quarter.

news.headline: ChatGPT ads reach 89 countries
news.what: OpenAI says more than 100,000 advertisers have run ChatGPT ads. Separately, NPR found ChatGPT citing look-alike local news sites that were really political ads.
news.why: ChatGPT is becoming a paid channel too, and it can be fooled about sources. A real, consistent presence across trusted sites is what protects your reputation in AI answers.

news.headline: Private chats that skip personalization
news.what: AI Mode added temporary threads that stay out of search history and don't use past searches to shape answers.
news.why: In those chats, everyone gets the same answer, so a business has to earn the recommendation on its own signals, not on a customer's history.

playbook_title: Five moves for the first quarter of 2027

playbook.title: Claim your ChatGPT business profile.
playbook.body: At chatgpt.com/business-hub. Match your Google profile word for word.

playbook.title: Treat your Google profile as AI's script.
playbook.body: Exact hours, services and booking. Tell staff an AI may call about availability.

playbook.title: Answer the long questions on your site.
playbook.body: Give each service, price range and service area its own clear answer.

playbook.title: Grow reviews beyond Google.
playbook.body: Yelp, industry directories and other trusted sites all feed what AI says about you.

playbook.title: Measure mentions, not just clicks.
playbook.body: Track whether AI names you, and compare results before and after the November update.
